sentences.zh: 有长门亭。前書文帝出長門，若見五人於道北，立五帝壇。

translations.literal: There is Changmen Pavilion. The Former Han says Emperor Wen went out through Changmen and seemed to see five men north of the road, so he established the Five Emperors altar.
translations.idiomatic: Changmen Pavilion stands here. The Former Han says Emperor Wen went out through Changmen and seemed to see five men north of the road, so he established the Five Emperors altar.

sentences.zh: 〖杜陵〗杜預曰古唐杜氏也。酆在西南。杜預曰：「在鄠縣東。」決錄注曰：「鎬在酆水東，酆在鎬水西，相去二十五里。」

translations.literal: Duling: Du Yu says this was the ancient Tang-Du clan. Feng lay to the southwest. Du Yu says, “It was east of Hu county.” The commentary to the Juelu says, “Hao was east of the Feng River, and Feng was west of Hao; they were twenty-five li apart.”
translations.idiomatic: Duling: Du Yu identifies it with the ancient Tang-Du clan. Feng lay to the southwest. Du Yu says, “It was east of Hu county.” The commentary to the Juelu says, “Hao was east of the Feng River, and Feng was west of Hao; they were twenty-five li apart.”

sentences.zh: 〖郑〗史記殺商君鄭黽池。鄭桓公封於此。黃圖云：「下邽縣並鄭，桓帝西巡復之。」

translations.literal: Zheng: the Records of the Historian says Lord Shang was killed at Zheng Mianchi. Duke Huan of Zheng was enfeoffed here. The Huangtu says, “Xiagui county annexed Zheng; when Emperor Huan made his western tour, he restored it.”
translations.idiomatic: Zheng: the Records of the Historian says Lord Shang was killed at Zheng Mianchi. Duke Huan of Zheng was enfeoffed here. The Huangtu says, “Xiagui county annexed Zheng; when Emperor Huan made his western tour, he restored it.”

sentences.zh: 〖新丰〗有骊山，杜預曰：「古驪戎國。」韋昭曰：「戎來居此山，故號驪戎。」三秦記曰：「始皇墓在山北，有始皇祠。不齋戒往，即疾風暴雨。人理欲上，則杳冥失道。縣西有白鹿原，周平王時白鹿出。」案關中圖，縣南有新豐原，白鹿在霸陵。东有鸿门亭。前書高帝見項羽處，孟康曰「在縣東七十里，舊大道北下阪口名」。關中記云始皇陵北十餘里有謝聚。及戏亭。周幽王死處，蘇林曰縣東南四十里。

translations.literal: Xinfeng: it had Li Mountain. Du Yu says, “It was the ancient Li Rong state.” Wei Zhao says, “The Rong came and dwelt on this mountain, so they were called the Li Rong.” The Sanqin ji says, “The First Emperor’s tomb is north of the mountain, and there is a shrine to the First Emperor. If one goes there without fasting and purification, there are violent winds and driving rain. When people intend to go up, it becomes dark and they lose the way. West of the county is White Deer Plain, where a white deer appeared in the time of King Ping of Zhou.” Note: according to the Guanzhong tu, south of the county was Xinfeng Plain, and White Deer was in Baling. To the east was Hongmen Pavilion. The Former Han says this was where Emperor Gao met Xiang Yu; Meng Kang says, “It was seventy li east of the county, the name of a lower slope-mouth north of the old main road.” The Guanzhong ji says Xie settlement was more than ten li north of the First Emperor’s mausoleum. Also there was Xi Pavilion, where King You of Zhou died; Su Lin says it was forty li southeast of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Xinfeng: Li Mountain was here. Du Yu says, “It was the ancient Li Rong state.” Wei Zhao says, “The Rong came and dwelt on this mountain, so they were called the Li Rong.” The Sanqin ji says, “The First Emperor’s tomb is north of the mountain, and there is a shrine to the First Emperor. If one goes there without fasting and purification, there are violent winds and driving rain. When people intend to go up, it becomes dark and they lose the way. West of the county is White Deer Plain, where a white deer appeared in the time of King Ping of Zhou.” Note: according to the Guanzhong tu, Xinfeng Plain lay south of the county, while White Deer was in Baling. Eastward was Hongmen Pavilion, where the Former Han says Emperor Gao met Xiang Yu; Meng Kang says, “It was seventy li east of the county, the name of a lower slope-mouth north of the old main road.” The Guanzhong ji says Xie settlement was more than ten li north of the First Emperor’s mausoleum. Xi Pavilion, where King You of Zhou died, was also here; Su Lin says it was forty li southeast of the county.

translations.literal: Thirteen cities; households 37,090; mouths 145,195. Pan Yue’s Guanzhong ji says, “The old seats of the Three Metropolitan Offices were in the city of Chang’an, while the senior officials each governed the people from their county offices. After Guangwu made his eastern capital, Fufeng went out to govern from Huaili, and Fengyi went out to govern from Gaoling.”

Pan Yue’s Guanzhong ji says, “The old offices of the Three Metropolitan commanderies were inside Chang’an, while their senior officials governed the people from their county seats. After Guangwu established the eastern capital, Fufeng moved its seat out to Huaili, and Fengyi moved its seat out to Gaoling.”

translations.literal: Chiyang: among the ten marshes of the Erya, Zhou had Jiaohuo; Guo Pu says it was Huzhong in this county. The Didiao ji says, “There was Mount Jienie to the north. There was Ghost Valley, where the three Suo clans arose.” Note: the Records of the Historian places Ghost Valley in Yangcheng in Yingchuan, differing from the geographical record.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyang: the Erya lists ten great marshes, and Zhou’s was Jiaohuo; Guo Pu identifies it with Huzhong in this county. The Didiao ji says, “There was Mount Jienie to the north. There was Ghost Valley, where the three Suo clans arose.” Note: the Records of the Historian puts Ghost Valley in Yangcheng, Yingchuan, which differs from this geographical record.
